q: 1. Which of the following is the correct statement for dimensioning a view?
options: All of them should be placed within a view
All of them should be placed close to the parts being dimensioned
They should be marked from visible outlines rather than from hidden line
Dimensions indicated in one view may be repeated in another view
explain: Good dimensioning practice requires dimensions to be taken/marked from visible outlines rather than from hidden (dashed) lines, since hidden-line dimensions are less reliable and clear.

q: 2. The dimension lines are marked in a building drawing with .............
explain: In building drawings, dimension line terminators are conventionally shown using either arrowheads or oblique ticks (short diagonal strokes), so 'arrows or ticks' is correct.

q: 3. The line connecting a view to note is called .............
explain: A leader line is a thin line (often ending in an arrowhead or dot) used to connect a note, label, or dimension to the specific feature it refers to on the drawing.

q: 4. Which type of line has precedence over all other types of lines?
explain: Per line-precedence conventions in drafting, a visible (continuous, outline) line always takes precedence over hidden lines and center lines when they coincide on a drawing.

q: 5. In an engineering drawing, dimension should be expressed in .............
explain: For clarity and consistency, engineering drawing convention requires all dimensions on a single drawing to be expressed in one unit only (typically millimeters), avoiding mixed units.

q: 6. Which of following publications made by Bureau of Indian Standards includes standard techniques for line conventions and lettering in detail?
explain: SP 46 (Engineering Drawing Practice for Schools and Colleges), published by the Bureau of Indian Standards, is the comprehensive reference document detailing line conventions, lettering standards, and other drawing practices.
As per standard line-type conventions, center lines are drawn as long-dashed dotted (chain) narrow lines, distinguishing them visually from continuous outlines and dashed hidden lines.

q: 8. Which of the following is not a specified method for dimensioning?
explain: Standard dimensioning methods include parallel (chain from a common baseline), continuous (chain, end-to-end), and coordinate dimensioning; 'perpendicular dimensioning' is not a recognized standard method.
A fillet is the term for a rounded interior corner (concave curve) at the junction of two surfaces, as opposed to a 'round' which refers to a rounded exterior/convex corner.

q: 10. Working drawing are also referred to as .............
explain: Working drawings, being the detailed drawings used directly for building/manufacturing, are also commonly referred to as construction drawings.

q: 11. The drawing constructed after completion of the construction work is .............
explain: An as-built drawing is specifically prepared after construction is complete, recording the actual final condition of the built structure, including any deviations from the original design.

q: 12. Section lining is drawn with line at .............
explain: As per standard hatching conventions, section lining (hatching) is typically drawn at 45° to the main outline/axis of the sectioned part.

q: 13. Working drawings are prepared at the stage of .............
explain: Working drawings, containing full dimensions and construction details, are produced during the detail design stage, after the concept has been finalized and before construction execution.

q: 14. The set of technical drawings used during the manufacturing phase of a product including civil construction are known as .............
explain: Working drawings are, by definition, the complete technical drawing set used during the actual manufacturing/construction phase of a product or building.

q: 15. Hatching line is a line which makes an angle of 45° with .............
explain: Standard hatching convention draws section lines at 45° to the main outline or principal axis of the sectioned component, rather than to a fixed horizontal/vertical reference.

q: 16. The representation of any matter by some sign or marks on the drawing is known as .............
explain: Standardized signs, symbols, or marks used to represent specific materials, features, or information on a drawing are collectively called conventions.

q: 17. Minimum area of opening for natural ventilation in patient room of hospital and class room is ............. of room area.
explain: Building ventilation norms in this reference specify that the minimum openable area for natural ventilation in hospital patient rooms and classrooms should be at least 1/6 of the room's floor area.
